articles.title: Canada stops using 'avalanche dogs' for rescues in Rocky Mountains, stirring outrage
articles.summary: A 55-year-old dog rescue programme that has found missing hikers and children in the Canadian wilderness was axed as part of government budget cuts.

blocks.text: Scott Ward can still recall the relief he saw on parents' faces when a search and rescue dog he was working with found their children safe in Canada's vast and heavily wooded Banff National Park.
Another time, his canine partner led him hiking up a steep mountainside for two hours until they reached a man with a broken leg who was close to dying from hypothermia.
Now 73 and retired, Ward spent 17 years as a dog handler in the wilderness of the Canadian Rocky Mountains, work he described as gratifying.
Over the years, the rescue programme was cut back to just one person in the role, and Ward was shocked when he heard recently that Parks Canada will end the programme entirely as of this month.
Prime Minister Mark Carney's government is making broad funding cuts to Canada's public service, and Parks Canada announced last week that hundreds of their employees will soon be laid off.

The agency confirmed the news to the BBC, calling it a "difficult decision" to axe its sole dog handler position out of Banff National Park, one of the most rugged parts of Canada that welcomes more than four million visitors each year from around the world.
It added it is part of its efforts to modernise its law enforcement branch, and that "search and rescue operations will continue to be delivered" through other means.
Cutting this one role has stirred public outrage, with more than 5,000 people signing a petition since Tuesday to restore it.
William Stevenson, the Conservative Member of Parliament for the Banff area who started the petition, says he welcomes tighter government spending, but that this cut could harm public safety.
"How could they possibly make such a bad choice in where to cut?" he told the BBC.
The BBC has asked Parks Canada about how much the canine search and rescue programme cost to administer.
For 55 years, the government used rescue dogs in the Canadian Rocky Mountains who were trained to trace "everything", Ward said, from a small paper clip to shell casings to a human body.
After avalanches, a common winter hazard in the area, they were called upon to search for trapped hikers or skiers underneath heavy mounds of snow.
"It saves probers hours and hours of standing shoulder to shoulder and poking in the snow, and also exposing themselves to secondary avalanche hazards," Ward said.
In the summer, they helped find children who got lost, often after wandering away from their parents' campsites.
"We lost a huge public safety and staff safety resource," he said.
Other countries still rely on canines, often called "avalanche dogs", for mountain search and rescue, including Italy, external.
The last dog in Parks Canada's programme, a German Shephard named Leroy, was retired in August.
For the seven years that he was on the job, Leroy helped track 156 people, find 57 who were lost in the wilderness, and solve two murders in Banff.

A new canine was trained and ready for duty before Parks Canada gave notice last week that the programme would be eliminated as part of recent C$145m ($104m; £78m) budget cuts to Parks Canada, local newspaper Rocky Mountain Outlook reported.
Along with his petition, Stevenson also raised the issue in Canada's parliament during a late sitting on Thursday.

In response, Ryan Turnball, a Liberal MP and the parliamentary secretary for finance, said the government is focused on reducing Canada's deficit and "ensuring public funds support growth, resilience and the well-being of Canadians".
Stevenson said he will continue to push on the issue, and has asked for a sit-down meeting with Parks Canada's CEO.
As for Ward, he hopes that the programme will soon be restored.

He recalled a quote that was often uttered by an old park warden who trained him: "You can make an armpit smell like a lilac bush and you can put a man on the moon, but nothing can replace the nose of the avalanche dog."

articles.title: PITX: Bicol-bound bus trips continue despite Mayon eruption
articles.summary: Despite Mayon Volcano's eruption on Friday morning, bus trips bound for Bicol from the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) remain uninterrupted.

blocks.text: Published October 31, 2026 12:51am
Despite Mayon Volcano's eruption on Friday morning, bus trips bound for Bicol from the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) remain uninterrupted.

In a "24 Oras" report by Jonathan Andal, PITX said six out of every 10 buses bound for Bicol were already fully booked. However, walk-in passengers could still be accommodated on ordinary and air-conditioned buses with available seats.
While some Bicol-bound passengers expressed concern over Mayon's eruption, they still pushed through with their trips. Others, meanwhile, were unaware of the volcanic activity.
“Nakakapagalala kasi wala po kaming balita talaga na pumutok pala yung bulkan. Hangga’t mayroon pong bumabyahe, parang tutuloy po kami,” said Daisy Belga, a passenger bound for Albay.
(It's worrying because we had no idea that the volcano had erupted. But as long as buses are still operating, we will push through with our trip.)
“Kinakabahan, pero mostly kasi tagilid naman kami, [sa] Polangui. Medyo gilid man pero abot kami ng ashfall,” added Virgie Magalona, another passenger bound for Albay.
(I'm nervous, but we're somewhat off to the side in Polangui. Even though we're not directly in the affected area, ashfall can still reach us.)
In Andal's report, a bus company said its drivers traveling to Bicol had reported no problems along their routes. However, driver Lito Rodriguez said he would remain cautious.
“Medyo delikado. Magpapa-ano na lang, magpapababa muna ng abo,” Rodriguez said.
(It's somewhat dangerous. I'll just wait for the ash to settle first.)
PITX said buses with online reservation systems were already fully booked, but many buses without online booking options continued to operate even without full passenger loads.
Since October 25, PITX has recorded more than one million passengers.
The terminal's security personnel have also confiscated hundreds of prohibited items, including pointed objects and flammable materials.
Passengers heading to their hometowns brought various types of luggage, with some even traveling with their pets.
PITX said pets are generally allowed on buses with their owners, provided they comply with the requirements.
“Usually ina-allow ng mga buses natin. Dapat po may cage, vaccination card at siyempre diaper po,” PITX Deputy Spokesperson Kolyn Gervacio-Calbasa said.
(Our buses generally allow pets, provided they are in cages and have vaccination cards and diapers.)
Meanwhile, large crowds of passengers have also started gathering at the Five Star bus terminal in Cubao, Quezon City, with some trips bound for Cagayan already fully booked.

Victory Liner has increased its trips to Baguio to 250 from the previous 150, as it expects passenger volume on the route to double to 10,000 starting October 31, 2026. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Tennessee woman Christa Pike describes pain after failed execution
articles.summary: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee. Her lawyers want her death sentence reduced to life, while the state governor has ordered an…

image.caption: Pike was convicted of murdering her classmate (FILE: 04/12/2007)Image: J. Miles Cary/Knoxville News Sentinel/USA TODAY NETWORK/REUTERS

blocks.text: Death row inmate Christa Pike said Friday that she remained in constant pain and struggled to speak a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee.
Her lawyers have urged Governor Bill Lee to reduce her death sentence to life imprisonment, but he has indicated that it will remain unchanged unless the courts intervene.
In her first public statement since the failed execution, Pike said she had expected to die but instead woke up alone and confused in a hospital bed.
"There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," she said. "My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak."
What happened during the execution attempt?

Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital during the September 30 execution attempt. Her lawyers said her arms were left burned and blistered. She spent the first few days in hospital unconscious and on a ventilator.
Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on whether a problem with the intravenous line caused the drug to collect in surrounding tissue rather than enter her bloodstream.
Newly released 911 calls reveal chaotic response to save Christa Pike
Lee ordered an investigation and postponed Tennessee's other lethal injection scheduled this year. The state's prison chief resigned.
What did Pike say?
Pike blamed the failed execution on "incompetence" and said her suffering extended beyond her physical injuries.
"There is pain in my mind and in my soul," she said.
She also expressed gratitude to the medical workers who saved her life and acknowledged the suffering of her victim's family.
Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and killing of her 19-year-old classmate Colleen Slemmer. Pike was 18 at the time of the crime, which she committed with her boyfriend.
"I continue to think about my victim's family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured," she said.
What happens next?
Lee told reporters this week: "I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts."
Pike dictated her statement to her legal team from the infirmary at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she returned after hospitalization.
"I don't know why I survived that night. I don't know what comes next," she said. "For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time."

articles.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
articles.summary: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.

blocks.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist.

The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider.
Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit.
The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds.

America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI.
The company also told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss".
Binance had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected".
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
A lot of the fear right now from Binance users - and the crypto industry at large - is whether or not Binance will actually be capable of covering this enormous financial loss.
The company has said repeatedly that customer funds will be covered and that the firm is strong enough to weather the storm.

But crypto history watchers have been pointing out online that this is exactly the kind of message that FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried gave before his crypto exchange collapsed in 2022, leading to huge losses for customers and the industry.
Binance has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
Meanwhile, AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said that several elements of the attack resembled earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
In the last five years the crypto industry has been beset by enormous losses from hackers.

In nearly all cases investigators have blamed hackers from North Korea, pointing to the infamous Lazarus Group - also know as TraderTraitor. The names refer to clusters of cyber criminals accused of working directly for the regime.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, said it had "high confidence" that a North Korean is linked to the hack.
North Korea is an impoverished country with very little industry and heavy international sanctions and experts say the regime uses cyber crime as a way to bring money in.
North Korea has always denied this, but the wealth of evidence from cryptocurrency flow analysis and insider interviews from defectors is compelling.
It makes North Korea likely to be the only nation that uses hacking as a way to raise public funds.

articles.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
articles.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

image.caption: Siarhei Tsikhanouski and his wife Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya in the European parliament in October 2025Image: Philipp von Ditfurth/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Blogger and dissident Siarhei Tsikhanouski , 48, was detained in Belarus in May 2020, after he had announced to challenge the country's ruler, Alexander Lukashenko, in the upcoming presidential elections. In December 2021, Tsikhanouski was convicted to 18 years in prison, in part for organizing "mass unrest."

After his arrest his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, took his place and challenged Lukashenko as presidential candidate. Despite allegations of large-scale vote-rigging, Lukashenko was declared the winner of the election in August 2020. This triggered unprecedented mass protests across the country. They were violently suppressed, and thousands of government critics were arrested or fled into exile. Tsikhanouskaya also fled her homeland and became the leading representative of the Belarusian democratic movement.
In June 2025, Siarhei Tsikhanouski was released after nearly five years in prison and was forcibly taken out of the country.
Blogger in exile

Some 14 months after his release, the blogger has re-activated his YouTube channel, where he not only denounces Alexander Lukashenko's regime, but also Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya's office, Belarusian media in exile, political analysts and others. Thousands of people follow his streams.

In one of them, Tsikhanouski claims that while Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya obviously enjoyed "a certain legitimacy from the European Union," the people who were living "quietly and silently" in Belarus today had not granted her any. He said that many of those who had voted for her as joint candidate of Belarus' opposition were regretting this today.
What does Tsikhanouski propose?

Tsikhanouski has suggested that a supervisory board should be established under the label "United Office of Demoratic Forces." It would be made up of "former presidential candidates, protest leaders and iconic figures of the revolution," including himself and his wife. "There would not be a full legitimacy but one which was at least granted by Belarusians," Tsikhanouski said, adding that such a supervisory board could oversee the distribution of grant funds.

blocks.caption: Speaking in the Czech senate in 2021, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya holds up a photo of her husbandImage: Vondrou Roman/CTK/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Speaking about his wife, he said: "Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya was a so-called technical candidate, who received the votes of all those who were against Lukashenko. The percentage of votes she received in the 2020 election was negligible because no one knew who she was. She was allowed to run because she did not pose a threat for the regime, and because she had neither supporters nor political experience."
What's happening in the Tsikhanouski family?

Asked by DW what his goals were, Siarhei Tsikhanouski refused to comment and referred to his livestreams instead. The former political prisoner is residing in the US and is, by his own account, currently unemployed. At the beginning of summer he said he was living in Los Angeles, learning English, preparing for university studies and writing a book. It is also known that his children — a teenage son and a younger daughter — temporarily stayed with him in the US. Today, however, they attend school in Poland, where Tsikhanouskaya resides.

Neither she nor her office have commented on the family situation or her husband's allegations. Even before the public dispute, the leader of the Belarusian democratic forces avoided commenting on her husband. Asked about his activities, she often suggested to approach him directly.

Speaking to DW in December 2025, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya merely said: "What happens in the public sphere and what happens at home, are different things. I understand Siarhei's deep traumatization and also his very strong reactions to certain events. Siarhei was in prison for five years, and I look at it with great understanding. This is why I'm not going public or making any comments. We'll deal with it among ourselves."
Democratic forces in a leadership crisis?

During the 32-year-long rule of the Lukashenko regime, the Belarusian opposition has weathered many crises and conflicts. Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya's leadership role has been called into question more than once. However, she and her team have always managed to work themselves out of difficult situations during the last couple of years. But will she still be able to do that now, with her own husband having turned into her critic?

Siarhei Tsikhanouski had gone back to his own self, said political scientist Yury Drakakhrust: "With all his idiosyncrasies, his style of debate, which is not exactly in line with common practice. This is likely to strike many as odd, including Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya's international partners."

Tsikhanouski, Drakakhrust pointed out, insisted that he was the key figure of the 2020 events, which is why he was entitled to all the benefits, privileges, recognition and invitations. But there was no way back.

"Even if we assume that Tsikhanouski is right, that he was the central figure, what good would it do today?" he asked. "If, suddenly, hundreds of thousands of Belarusians watched his livestreams, collected funds, formed local groups or associations in Tsikhanouski's name, then perhaps it would be possible to turn back the wheel. But this will hardly be the case."

blocks.caption: Siarhei Tsikhanouski and Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya at a rally organized by Belarusian diaspora in Warsaw in June 2025Image: Czarek Sokolowski/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Drakakhrust described the current situation within the democratic forces as a "crisis." He doubted that Tsikhanouski would be able to reach an agreement with all the members of the supervisory board he has proposed. Furthermore, his wife, in particular, had since established certain assets, resources, and a status for herself through her office.
Tsikhanouskaya — recognized beyond Belarusian borders

"Tsikhanouskaya is being received at high levels, if not as an elected president, then as a leader for Belarus and Belarusian democracy. She's not regarded as just one of several democratic leaders from Belarus," the political scientist said.

He pointed out that not only Tsikhanouskaya, but also other actors from the 2020 election campaign are in exile. They, however, had not achieved a similar level of representation or comparable access to resources. "She has surpassed them as a politician, and that's what counts."

Drakakhrust said that the Belarusian government views disputes among the opposition with a touch of irony, occasionally adding fuel to the fire: "Basically, they don't care who wins. The main thing is that there is conflict, bickering and mutual vilification."
This article was originally published in Russian.

articles.title: US midterms: Pope Leo XIV casts vote by mail
articles.summary: As a US citizen, Pope Leo XIV is eligible to vote in US elections and has made use of that right with a postal ballot ahead of Tuesday's midterms. The pontiff, a Chicago native, did not reveal who he…

image.caption: Pope Leo XIV is a politically outspoken pontiff and has criticized US President Donald TrumpImage: Ciro De Luca/REUTERS

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV has become the first ever pontiff to vote in a United States general election after submitting a mail-in ballot ahead of November's midterms, the Vatican confirmed on Friday.
The 71-year-old US citizen, who was born in Chicago, Illinois, as Robert Francis Prevost, applied for a postal vote on October 3, according to US media.
The Holy See's press office said in a statement that the pope "has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen" and has done so "whenever he was eligible to do so."
Indeed, records held by the Illinois State Board of Elections show that Robert Prevost has voted in every general election since 2000 except those in 2020 and 2022, including five primary elections.
Through his time as a bishop in Peru, Pope Leo also holds Peruvian citizenship and the Vatican said he had also voted whenever eligible while living in the South American country.

"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," said a spokesperson in Vatican City, which itself is an absolute monarchy and does not hold political elections.
Pope Leo XIV. warns of 'new senseless slaughter' in Europe
Pope Leo XIV: Do we know who the pontiff voted for?
In Tuesday's US midterm elections, all seats in the House of Representatives and about one third of the Senate are set to be contested.
US President Donald Trump's Republicans are seeking to defend narrow majorities in both chambers against a strong challenge from the Democrats.
In Illinois, voters are deciding whether to elect Governor JB Pritzker for a third term, and are also filling an open US Senate seat after the retirement of longtime Catholic Democrat Dick Durbin.
It remains unclear who Pope Leo has voted for but the pontiff has repeatedly clashed with President Trump and his administration since the start of his pontificate a year and a half ago.
Leo has criticized Trump on issues such as the Iran war, migration and press freedom and declined an invitation to the United States' 250th anniversary celebrations earlier this year.
The two are yet to meet personally but Trump has often attacked the pontiff personally, calling him "weak" and captive to the "radical left."
"I'm not afraid of the Trump administration or of speaking out loudly about the message of the Gospel, which is what the church works for," Leo responded while on a trip to Algeria in April.
"I will continue to speak out strongly against war, seeking to promote peace, promoting dialogue and multilateralism among states to find solutions to problems."
Can Pope Leo move President Trump on the Iran war?

MANILA, Philippines — On its second edition in the Philippines, the Michelin Guide recognized 19 new food establishments across Manila, Cebu, Pampanga and Cavite, bringing the number of honorees this year to 127.
The new additions across Manila, Cebu, Pampanga and Cavite were cited by the gastronomy recognition body for their world-class culinary identity.

“Manila continues to lead with chef-driven restaurants, tasting menus, and ambitious contemporary concepts, while Cebu draws strength from its lechon, seafood, charcoal-grilled dishes, and convivial home cooking,” the Michelin Guide said.

Makati-based restaurant Helm retained its two-Michelin stars, while Asador Alfonso, Celera, Gallery by Chele, Hapag, Inatô, Kása Palma, Linamnam and Toyo Eatery maintained its one-Michelin star distinction.

Flow in Makati joined the guide with a one-star distinction for the extensive use of local ingredients that create “varied textures and layered sauces to craft flavors that are innovative and harmonious.”
Meanwhile, Michelin recognized 31 establishments as Bib Gourmand up from its 25 awardees last year.

Among the new Bib Gourmand food places are Apag Marangle and Tito Boy in Pampanga, Balay Dako and Bawai’s Vietnamese Kitchen in Cavite, Azela in Manila, Tatang’s Lechon and Kalipay in Cebu and C.H.E Bacolod Chicken House Express in Makati.
Ato-ah in Cebu and Butcher Boy in Las Piñas were promoted to Bib Gourmand from the Selected list last year.
Under the Michelin Selected, 86 establishments were named this year, up from 74 in the inaugural edition.

The 18 newly recognized were Abé (Taguig), Bombvinos Bodega, Cyria’s Kandingan, Digámo, Elaia by Cyma, Haliya, Idalia, Kokeek’s Manokan, Kong, Kumedor, Liyab, Makanai, Marjo’s Pochero, Mila’s Tokwa’t Baboy (San Andres), Oyster Bay, Playa, Souq and Tadhanà.

Michelin also awarded former overseas Filipino worker Chef Frances Tariga of Tadhanà with the Opening of the Year recognition and former seafarer Chef Francis Lacson of Digámo with the Young Chef award.
Chef Clyde Joshua Zafra of Tito Boy received the service award while bar beverage manager Ron Job Sanchez of Automat was given the Exceptional Cocktails Award.
In a speech, President Marcos said the government will support culinary education for aspiring chefs and hospitality professionals to strengthen the industry.

articles.title: P30 million cloud-seeding brings hope to Visayas sugar farms
articles.summary: As the Visayas sugar industry braces for the looming threat of a projected super El Niño, a much-needed dose of hope may soon come from the skies.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

The Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) is setting aside P30 million for cloud-seeding operations in the Visayas, particularly in Negros Island and Panay, to help ease the impact of prolonged dry conditions on sugarcane farms.
STAR / File
BACOLOD CITY, Philippines — As the Visayas sugar industry braces for the looming threat of a projected super El Niño, a much-needed dose of hope may soon come from the skies.
United Sugar Producers Federation (UNIFED) president Manuel Lamata said he received a letter from SRA administrator Pablo Luis Azcona, dated Oct. 26, confirming the funds have been allocated.
The cloud-seeding operations are expected to begin this November.
Lamata expressed gratitude to Azcona for taking early action, saying the industry hopes the funding will be enough to help sugar farmers weather the difficult months ahead.

Lamata thanked Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel for funding cloud-seeding operations last month and for announcing the Department of Agriculture will provide additional funding for similar efforts next year.
For sugarcane farmers already facing drought, pest infestation and rising fuel and farm-input costs, every drop of rain could make a difference.
Lamata said the actions of Azcona and Laurel demonstrate their concern for the sugar industry, particularly during a challenging period for farmers and workers.

articles.title: VP camp calls out new ‘tanim witness’
articles.summary: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte yesterday dismissed the claim of an alleged former driver of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, that he delivered suitcases of cash to her.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte arrives before the start of the impeachment trial at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on July 7, 2026.
AFP / Noel Celis

MANILA, Philippines — The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte yesterday dismissed the claim of an alleged former driver of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, that he delivered suitcases of cash to her.

Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo reacted after the former driver of Velasco, identified with the alias “Chris,” arrived at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Thursday to submit his affidavit against Duterte.

“Another day, another tanim (planted) witness. They can keep manufacturing allegations, but they cannot fabricate the truth,” Panelo said in a statement. “As before, VP Sara will happily dismantle each allegation with evidence at the proper time.”
The spokesperson also asked the media not merely to report, but to independently test and verify these claims.
“That way, they can see for themselves how the Fourth Estate is being weaponized for the relentless, but ultimately ineffective, black propaganda against the Vice President,” Panelo added.
In his affidavit, Chris said he allegedly delivered suitcases of money twice to Duterte in Davao from 2021 to 2022 upon Velasco’s instruction.

Prior to this, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. said he delivered more than P2 billion in cash to Duterte and members of her family on the instructions of Velasco. The Vice President and other people named in the claims have denied the allegations.
Melvin Matibag, NBI director, said yesterday they will summon Chris to verify his account and supporting evidence.
He said Chris submitted an affidavit and photographs linking him to trips to Davao City in 2021 and 2022. His account could corroborate Gracioso’s allegations.
“He is one of the drivers mentioned as having accompanied Gracioso,” Matibag said in an interview over True FM.

The NBI chief said investigators would examine the witness’s photographs, social media posts and other possible evidence before making recommendations. He added the bureau would summon Chris for further questioning and ask whether he would agree to undergo a polygraph examination.
Matibag said the witness reportedly received at least P150,000 per delivery, but clarified that he had yet to personally review the affidavit.

Chris, who appeared before the NBI on Thursday, told reporters that he joined two trips to Davao, transporting an estimated 15 suitcases each time. He said their head driver told him the luggage contained a “small gift” for Duterte.
However, Chris admitted that he did not know what the suitcases contained and never saw the Vice President. He said he and the other drivers were left outside the destination.
Matibag said the new witness’s account appeared consistent with some details disclosed by Gracioso, but stressed the NBI would carefully validate the information before reaching conclusions.

The bureau also plans to invite Velasco and other people mentioned in the allegations to clarify their involvement. Matibag said immigration records indicated that Velasco was last reported to be in Japan, with investigators checking information that he may be in the Niseko area. — Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: Diokno: Concrete plan needed amid peso drop
articles.summary: Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno urged the Marcos administration to present a clear and concrete plan to address the peso’s continued depreciation and cushion its impact on ordinary families.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
House prosecutor and Akbayan Representative Chel Diokno delivers his oral arguments before the Senate impeachment court on July 15, 2026.
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno urged the Marcos administration to present a clear and concrete plan to address the peso’s continued depreciation and cushion its impact on ordinary families.

Diokno said it is important that public assurances are matched by decisive action and practical measures to manage the economic challenges and mitigate the effects of rising prices on household budgets.

“Apart from advice, what the people are waiting for is the government’s swift action to lessen the effects of continued increase in prices of basic goods and the weak value of the peso,” he said in a statement.
He stressed that families already struggling to make ends meet need clear answers on what the government will do to help them cope with rising living costs.
“The government must lay out clear, concrete measures to address these economic pressures and ease the burden on ordinary households,” Diokno said.

“Every time the peso weakens and prices rise, families can afford less with what they earn. The government must act to protect their purchasing power and ensure that basic necessities remain within reach,” he said.
The Philippine peso has fallen to historic levels of over P64 versus the US dollar.

articles.title: How tech can help Filipinos weather El Niño impact
articles.summary: From low-cost water filtration systems to biofertilizers and automated irrigation, Filipino-made technologies are offering practical solutions to water shortages and agricultural losses as the…

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — From low-cost water filtration systems to biofertilizers and automated irrigation, Filipino-made technologies are offering practical solutions to water shortages and agricultural losses as the country braces for the impact of a “super” El Niño.
The Department of Agriculture has reported P8.6 billion in crop losses, underscoring the need for measures to help farmers cope with prolonged dry conditions.
In response, Filipino innovators are developing homegrown technologies and practical solutions to help communities adapt to its effects.
Biochar filter
One such innovation is a biochar water filter developed by Sambali Beach Farm, a social enterprise in Zambales that uses charcoal recycled from discarded young coconuts, or buko.
The filtration system uses charcoal, cleaned sand and stones to filter water through a series of drums, making it suitable for drinking. The four-drum setup costs P4,800 and can be used for one year.
The enterprise has donated filtration systems to Aeta communities in Zambales, where water stations are scarce. Subdivision owners and farmers have also adopted the technology to reduce costs.

“Actually, we made this for disaster response, so local government units (LGUs) should have this,” Jeanet Delfierro, a community organizer at Sambali Beach Farm, said on the sidelines of the “Handa Pilipinas Luzon Leg” in Clark, Pampanga, an initiative of the Department of Science and Technology. “Whenever there are disasters, they can bring this to areas with no source of water.
“They can get water from the pump or the river and put it in there. It will be filtered and you don’t have to spend millions of pesos,” she added.
To demonstrate the filter’s effectiveness, Sambali Beach Farm uses it in its restaurant, where foreign visitors also drink the filtered water, Delfierro said.

The enterprise supports 500 households across the Zambales provincial capital of Iba and the towns of Botolan, Cabangan, Palauig and San Felipe. Delfierro hopes to secure more funding to expand its operations to other towns in the province.
Nutrio biofertilizer

Aside from addressing water shortages, the DOST is scaling up technologies to help farmers cope with El Niño through Project SARAI, or Smarter Approaches to Reinvigorate Agriculture as an Industry in the Philippines, which has received continuing appropriations of P600 million since 2025.
Among the technologies being promoted is Nutrio, a biofertilizer developed by researchers from the University of the Philippines Los Baños.
Made with microorganisms, the product helps crops such as sugarcane achieve better yields at a lower cost.
Marlon Gamboa, a farmer from Paniqui, Tarlac, took a chance on the biofertilizer two years ago at Ruby’s Farm to reduce his reliance on conventional urea fertilizer.
“More than 50 percent of the cost of the fertilizer will be lost if you use Nutrio,” Gamboa told reporters during a visit in July.

Nutrio is being tested in seven provinces, including Tarlac. In a commercial trial in Concepcion, farmers who used Nutrio alongside urea harvested 69.25 tons of sugarcane per hectare, 23 percent above the national average. The trial also generated an additional income of P72,755.

Each bag of Nutrio costs P350, an added expense that Gamboa acknowledged. However, he said the benefits have been substantial, with Ruby’s Farm now harvesting an average of 125 tons of cane per hectare per cropping season, up from 30 to 40 tons previously.
Irrigation system
To further improve production and reduce water waste, Gamboa also adopted an automated furrow irrigation system developed by Central Luzon State University (CLSU).
The P400,000 system regulates the amount and timing of irrigation water, helping farmers avoid unnecessary water use.

“We have two soil moisture sensors: the first (sensor) will dictate when you will water the soil… When the sugarcane has consumed 50 percent of the available soil moisture, that’s when irrigation will begin,” Marvin Cinense, director of CLSU’s Philippine-Sino Center for Agricultural Technology, said during a demonstration.
“We do not need to water the sugarcane often. The sub-sensor will determine when it stops. That means we are reducing the losses,” he added.
Promoting solutions
Despite the potential benefits of local innovations, getting the public to adopt them remains a challenge.

One example is the Department of Social Welfare and Development’s water filtration kit, suggested by President Marcos, which drew ridicule from some Filipinos amid discussions about collecting rainwater to address El Niño.
DOST Secretary Renato Solidum Jr. defended the kit, saying its specialized bucket can collect rainwater and filter out particles to make the water for drinking.

articles.title: 2-year delay on CCTV turnover at NAIA irks Dizon
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon expressed dismay at the nearly two-year delay in the transfer of closed-circuit television control at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon expressed dismay at the nearly two-year delay in the transfer of closed-circuit television control at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.

During an inspection at the NAIA Terminal 1 yesterday as Undas approaches, Dizon was frustrated at how the transfer of CCTV control from the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) to the New NAIA Infrastructure Corp. (NNIC) has been delayed, citing safety concerns.
“The problem here is there’s no single accountability. Our problem is simple, someone was robbed and you are all pointing fingers,” the Department of Transportation chief said.
“We’ve been fixing the transfer since last year. I want this turnover done immediately. So, we will only scold one and you will not point fingers. Nothing will happen to us,” he added.
Dizon ordered the MIAA to turn over the responsibility, authority, and operations of all CCTV cameras to NNIC by November.
He warned the involved officials that they will be fired should they not beat the deadline.
In addition, Dizon ordered NNIC to add more CCTV cameras in every corner of the terminal in order to ensure the safety of passengers.
The inspection was triggered after a French tourist was robbed of three high-value timepieces worth millions.
Dizon said – with the assistance of Sen. Raffy Tulfo and his staff – the suspect was identified and the items were retrieved.
Around 1.2 million passengers are expected to flock NAIA terminals from Oct. 27 to Nov. 4.
On the other hand, Dizon lauded the other improvements of the terminals such as a renovated arrival area and automated immigration gates.
He noted that all Filipinos can access e-gates aside from overseas Filipinos workers and foreigners in order to avoid long lines.
According to the MIAA, they will complete the turnover of the CCTV surveillance system to the NNIC within November.

The MIAA has already completed the final acceptance of the CCTV project, and initiated the necessary arrangements for its formal turnover to NNIC in accordance with the NAIA Public-Private Partnership Concession Agreement.

Meanwhile, the MIAA continues its CCTV repair and restoration efforts, in coordination with Abratique & Associates Philippines Inc., while maintaining appropriate security measures to protect passengers and other airport users. — Rudy Santos

articles.title: BAN Toxics warns of chemicals in Halloween toys
articles.summary: A watchdog group has warned consumers about hazardous chemicals found in Halloween toys and costumes, urging manufacturers and importers to comply with Philippine safety standards to protect children…

blocks.text: October 31, 2026 | 12:00am
Shoppers browse Halloween toys and costumes at Divisoria Market in Manila on October 30, 2026 as Filipinos prepare for Halloween celebrations.
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — A watchdog group has warned consumers about hazardous chemicals found in Halloween toys and costumes, urging manufacturers and importers to comply with Philippine safety standards to protect children from toxic exposure.

In a statement released to Bulacan reporters, Thony Dizon, advocacy and campaign officer of BAN Toxics, cautioned the public against allowing toxic chemicals to turn trick-or-treating into a health hazard.

During a recent market monitoring and purchasing activity, BAN Toxics subjected various Halloween toys and costumes to chemical screening using a Vanta C Series HH XRF Analyzer. The tests detected lead content of up to 1,130 parts per million and cadmium levels of up to 160 ppm.

The group also reported that all the children’s Halloween items it monitored and inspected failed to meet the product labeling standards mandated by Republic Act 10620, or the Toy and Game Safety Labeling Act of 2013.

“Manufacturers and importers of these toys should comply with existing Philippine safety standards on chemical content and product labeling, which are mandatory to protect children from toxic exposure,” Dizon said.

He noted that the use of lead in the production and sale of toys is strictly prohibited under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources’ Administrative Order 2013-24, or the Chemical Control Order for Lead and Lead Compounds.

Republic Act 10620 also requires toy manufacturers to comply with labeling requirements, including the License to Operate number issued by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), age grading, cautionary statements and warnings, instructional literature, the manufacturer’s complete name and address, and the item model or Stock Keeping Unit number.
BAN Toxics urged the FDA and local government units to conduct post-market surveillance and confiscate unlabeled and unnotified toys and child care articles, including children’s Halloween products.

“Preventing the spread of unsafe children’s products in the market should be the core action not just of a single agency but a concerted effort by all stakeholders, including local government units and the general public,” the group said.

articles.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
articles.summary: Shares in Intel have continued to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.

blocks.text: US stocks have continued to slide as concerns continue to intensify over the increasing costs of the artificial intelligence (AI) build out.

Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.
Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.
The losses follow the value of Google owner Alphabet plunging by more than $500bn on Thursday after it revealed its own AI summaries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.
Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.
The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.
On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.
"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.
Reddit stock was down by 26%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.
Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by nearly 20%, as its daily active user numbers dropped.
Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI.
Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google.
He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out".
"The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down."

articles.title: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on Trump military aid decision
articles.summary: Chris Murphy said waiving a human rights condition on aid paved the way for arrests of journalists.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
US Senator Chris Murphy
ByTom Bateman
State department correspondent
A top Democratic senator has blamed a crackdown on independent journalism in Egypt on a decision by the Trump administration to waive human rights conditions on US military funding to the country.

Chris Murphy, who sits on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, accused the US government of "abandoning" the Egyptian people after it lifted restrictions relating to more than $300m of defence assistance.

Over the last month a series of arrests has taken place of journalists at two of the few remaining independent news outlets in Egypt, where newspapers and TV stations are closely controlled by the authorities.
The US State Department told the BBC it waived conditions on a portion of military aid to Egypt in September due to the country's "importance to US national security interests".
Murphy, speaking at the Middle East Institute (MEI) in Washington this week, said he was in no doubt the two were linked.
"The minute that money was released, the crackdown began in an absolutely devastating way," he said.
On Tuesday a court in Cairo ordered the closure of the news website Madr Masa and fined its editor-in-chief Lina Attalah in what Amnesty International called "a crushing blow to press freedom".
Earlier this month, authorities arrested six journalists at the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh and charged them with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
The Egyptian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

Cairo has remained a close regional ally of the US despite what human rights groups say are widespread abuses under President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's government, including torture and enforced disappearances.

Sisi denies there are political prisoners in Egypt. He has previously said stability and security are paramount, adding authorities have promoted rights by trying to provide basic needs such as jobs and housing.

blocks.caption: Image caption, US President Donald Trump at a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump at a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
Washington sends Egypt £1.3bn ($1.73bn) per year, making it one of the world's biggest recipients of US military assistance.

US law allows up to £320m of the funding to be withheld, conditioned on Egypt meeting democracy and human rights requirements. But these restrictions can be waived by the administration on national security grounds.

In September, Secretary of State Marco Rubio waived human rights conditions on $320m of military aid in light of Egypt's role since the launch of the US war with Iran, according to a letter addressed to various Congressional committees. Egypt assisted negotiations between the US and Iran.

Exercising the waiver authority was "essential" for the US-Egypt relationship, "particularly in light of Egypt's helpful role following Operation Epic Fury," according to the September 4 memo seen by Reuters which bore Rubio's signature.

Asked by the BBC about the move in light of this month's arrests of journalists, the State Department said the waiver was "due to Egypt's importance to US national security interests, the concrete security cooperation Egypt provides to the United States, and the need to maintain that cooperation to address regional security challenges".
It added it maintained dialogue with Cairo on a "full range of issues" but would "not comment on private diplomatic conversations".

blocks.caption: Image caption, Six journalists from the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh who were arrested in Egypt and are facing terrorism charges

blocks.text: Image source, Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights
Six journalists from the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh who were arrested in Egypt and are facing terrorism charges

Rubio's move followed a similar decision by the Biden administration in 2024, when then Secretary of State Anthony Blinken waived human rights conditions to grant the full military aid allocation to Egypt as the US sought Cairo's role in mediating between Israel and Hamas in the war in Gaza.
Under Biden prior to 2024, the US withheld portions of the annual military allocation over Egypt's human rights record.
Murphy, who chairs a congressional committee on the Middle East and counterterrorism, said he had been a critic of both the Biden and Trump administrations over the issue.

"To the extent that there was any glimmer left of political speech in Egypt, it is gone for one proximate reason: The United States government abandoned the people of Egypt and decided to remove all conditions on our funding," Murphy told the MEI.
"Any hope of a true, meaningful political opposition rebirthing in Egypt has been shattered by this decision," he added.

US military aid to Cairo began after the 1978 Camp David Accords and the peace treaty that followed between Egypt and Israel. Successive administrations have viewed the world's most populous Arab country as a critical US ally in the region.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Amnesty International called the verdict against Lina Attalah 'a crushing blow to press freedom' (file photo)

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Amnesty International called the verdict against Lina Attalah 'a crushing blow to press freedom' (file photo)
The group Reporters Without Borders describes Egypt, external as one of the world's biggest jailers of journalists.

The conviction of Lina Attalah and the closure of Madr Masr marked an unprecedented escalation in repression of press freedoms in Egypt, according to Timothy E Kaldas, Deputy Director of The Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, a Washington DC-based think tank.
He said both the US and European Union had been prioritising their strategic relations with Egypt over human rights and the rule of law in the country.
"It's been fostering a sense of impunity on the part of the Egyptian authorities that we're seeing play out," he told the BBC.
"Egypt is getting signals from both sides of the Atlantic that human rights and the rule of law are no longer a priority, and they're testing the limits of that."
He added: "The fact that they're not getting more robust pushback reinforces the wrong message."

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
articles.summary: The Chicago-born pontiff, who has a tense relationship with Trump, mailed in a ballot for the midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress.

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV has submitted his mail-in ballot in Illinois, for the midterm elections, becoming the first-ever pope to vote in a US election.
"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," the Holy See Press Office said in a statement.
The Chicago-born pontiff is the first US citizen to hold the Vatican's highest seat, after his selection in May 2025.
Since then, he has clashed with the Trump administration over various issues, including immigration enforcement and the US-Israel war with Iran.
"Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so," the press office said, including during his years in Peru.
The US midterm elections will determine which political party controls Congress and have a significant impact on the final years of Donald Trump's presidency.
Elections will be held nationwide on 3 November, but early voting has begun in most states.
According to NBC News, the Pope requested his mail-in ballot from the Will County Clerk's Office on 3 October.
Less than two weeks later, the Vatican announced he had surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung after he was diagnosed with lung cancer.
The Vatican confirmed last week that the Pope, aged 71, will travel as planned to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru in early November.
Tensions escalated between the Pope and the US president in April, after the Pope called for peace in the wake of US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
"I don't think he's doing a very good job," Trump said about the Pope afterwards.
"We don't like a Pope that's going to say that it's OK to have a nuclear weapon," he continued. "I'm not a big fan of Pope Leo."
Pope Leo followed with his own remarks later, saying: "The mission of the Church is to preach the Gospel, to preach peace," according to Reuters.
"If someone wants to criticise me for preaching the Gospel... I hope simply to be listened to because of the value of God's words."
In the final few days before the midterms, Republican and Democratic officials alike are sprinting across the country to boost their party's chances of success.

Polls suggest Democrats are the favourite to gain control of the lower chamber of Congress, called the House of Representatives, and are poised to win seats in Republican-leaning areas that overwhelmingly voted for Trump in the 2024 presidential election.
Democrats also appear to have a chance to win additional seats in the Senate, the upper chamber of Congress.
The gloomy outlook for Trump's Republican party has seen the president hold several rallies in states where Republican victories are typically all but guaranteed.

Merz at DMZ says he hopes Korea can reunify like Germany did

blocks.caption: Merz visited the "T2" barrack building at the DMZImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.
North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

blocks.caption: Merz briefly stepped into the 'North Korean side' behind a conference table in the border barrack buildingImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.
"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he said.

"You can also notice it here at this place, how much a country suffers from division and how strong the desire is for reunification, at least in this part of the Korean Peninsula," he said, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience while visiting Seoul.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state."

articles.title: ‘Amateur morons’: Flávio Bolsonaro’s short-lived ‘president-elect’ claim met with mockery
articles.summary:
Brazilian media ridicule defeated candidate over ‘shameful’ absconsion to US and bizarre letter with wrong coat of arms

Flávio Bolsonaro had hoped that by Sunday night people would be…
articles.byline: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro

blocks.text: Flávio Bolsonaro had hoped that by Sunday night people would be calling him the next president of Brazil.

Instead, the far-right politician’s decision to flee to the United States after losing the election and – for 58 minutes – declare himself “Brazil’s true president-elect”, has made him a laughing stock, with Brazilian newspapers and commentators raining a barrage of scornful adjectives down on the conquered candidate.

“If it served any purpose at all, Flávio’s foolishness liberated the democratic right from a family of coup-mongers, which for far too long held it hostage to their reckless folly and irremediable disdain for Brazil,” the conservative Estado de São Paulo newspaper thundered on Friday.

Bolsonaro fled to Miami on Tuesday, 48 hours after being beaten by his leftwing adversary, the incumbent president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, by 4.4m votes. Lula’s victory has been recognised by rightwing leaders from around the world, including El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele and Italy’s Giorgia Meloni, not to mention Bolsonaro’s own party and many key allies.

But on Wednesday after landing in the US, Bolsonaro published an outlandish letter – reportedly produced with the help of ChatGPT – in which he declared himself “the true president-elect of Brazil” and made phoney claims about election fraud.

Perhaps most bizarrely, the far-right absconder claimed he would continue to lead Brazil’s opposition from abroad, comparing himself to Charles de Gaulle, who in the 1940s led a French government-in-exile against the Nazis from London, and the Cuban independence hero José Martí, who challenged the Spanish empire from New York.

“They were all treated as criminals by the regimes they confronted. History called them something else,” Bolsonaro said, also likening himself to Venezuela’s Nobel laureate María Corina Machado and Rui Barbosa, a Brazilian politician who went into exile in London in the late 19th century after challenging an authoritarian president known as “the Iron Marshal”.

Just under an hour after Bolsonaro’s proclamation was first published on social media, a corrected version was issued, altering his claimed status to “leader of Brazil” – reportedly after he was upbraided by Trump administration officials keen to avoid a full-blown diplomatic split with Brazil’s actual leaders.

The amended letter also updated the out-of-date Brazilian coat of arms that had been used erroneously in the letterhead of the first version referring to the “United States of Brazil” – a name the South American country has not used since 1967.
Bolsonaro’s flight – and his brief but bogus claim to be “president-elect” of one of the world’s largest democracies – prompted a ferocious outpouring of opprobrium and ridicule.
“[This letter] seems to have been written by a foolhardy, loony halfwit,” Flávia Oliveira, a prominent political commentator, told the network GloboNews.

The Estado de São Paulo’s leader writers said: “Flávio’s letter isn’t worth the ink of this newspaper, but there’s no way the embarrassment can be ignored,” before savaging a man they called “a con artist of the highest order”.

blocks.caption: A woman reads a newspaper with news of the election result on Monday in São Paulo. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Rio broadsheet O Globo said Bolsonaro’s “shameful and sneaky” decision to abscond laid bare the “pathetic” nature of his political movement, Bolsonarismo, while the Folha de São Paulo said it exposed the true nature of the “authoritarian, ignorant, incompetent” Bolsonaro family.
José Casado, a columnist for the conservative magazine Veja, wrote: “The comedy storyline has already guaranteed him a spot in the pages of political satire.”
Merval Pereira, a conservative columnist for O Globo, called Bolsonaro “a madhouse Napoleon”.

Even Silas Malafaia, a pugnacious televangelist who is close to Bolsonaro’s jailed father, Jair Bolsonaro, had harsh words. “Bolsonaro’s kids are jackasses … A bunch of amateur morons,” Malafaia was quoted as saying by O Globo.

Some observers see Bolsonaro’s post-defeat getaway as proof that his dispirited movement is dead. “I think Bolsonarismo was defeated once and for all,” Lula’s chief foreign policy adviser, Celso Amorim, said this week, calling the result “the last gasp of a radical, irrational, lying rightwing”.

The Estado de São Paulo’s editorial board agreed. “Flávio belongs to the past and will soon vanish into the basement of political irrelevance from which he should never have emerged,” they predicted, urging conservatives to ditch Bolsonaro and throw their weight behind his ally Tarcísio de Freitas, the São Paulo governor.
Others warn Bolsonarismo will remain a powerful political force, even if the Bolsonaro family’s leadership of the far-right movement is now in doubt.

Social media users were also merciless in their reaction to Bolsonaro’s short-lived claim to be “president-elect”. One meme invited supporters to attend his January inauguration – at Cinderella Castle in Walt Disney World, Orlando. Another parodied his movement’s fascist-inspired slogan “God, Homeland and Family”, which became “Goodbye, Homeland and Family”.

Donald Trump has declined to publicly recognise the result of an election he has called “a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil”. But a US diplomatic cable obtained by the Folha de São Paulo called Lula’s victory “surprising but definitive”.
Asked if he saw Bolsonaro as Brazil’s “rightful” leader, Trump replied: “I won’t get involved.”

articles.title: Seoul fears being sidelined as US reaches out to North Korea
articles.summary: With ties between South Korea and the Trump administration strained, the South Korean government worries that Donald Trump's pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough with Kim Jong Un may come at Seoul's…

image.caption: South Korea has been facing pressure both from North Korea and from its ally, the United StatesImage: Evan Vucci/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: South Korea's relationship with the North, always strained, seems to be going through a particularly hostile patch in recent weeks.

Last month, Seoul accused North Korea of planting a mine on the southern side of the heavily fortified border. The device exploded, injuring three South Korean soldiers. Pyongyang refused to apologize and insisted this was a false-flag incident designed to tarnish the isolated nation. The North Korean regime has since conducted multiple weapons tests, held its first-ever exhibition of military drones attended by Kim Jong Un, brought up self-propelled artillery units to the border and started preparing loudspeaker systems that will blast propaganda into the South.
On Thursday, North Korea also fired around 10 short-range ballistic missiles towards the Sea of Japan just before a scheduled visit to South Korea by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

On top of South Korea's issues with its arch rival, many in Seoul are growing increasingly wary of their most important ally, the United States. South Korean politicians are worried that the US could push for a diplomatic breakthrough with North Korea at the cost of ignoring South Korea's security, or even leave it exposed to Pyongyang's nuclear arsenal.
Who gets a voice on South Korea's future?

US President Donald Trump famously claimed he and Kim Jong Un "fell in love" during Trump's first term. More recently, Trump has indicated he would like to resume talks . There have been suggestions that a meeting could take place on November 18 in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, where Trump is expected to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
Why North Korea is now Europe's problem

The North Korean side has made no official response to Washington's hints, although South Korea's National Intelligence Service informed a closed-door meeting of Seoul's intelligence committee on Thursday that Kim Jong Un discussed the possibility of meeting Trump when he met with senior members of China's politburo in Dandong on Saturday.

Seoul's fears were also fueled by the US proposing three-way talks with Russia and China on the fate of Ukraine without inviting a representative of Kyiv to attend. The worry in Seoul is that President Donald Trump may conduct a similar bypass manoeuvre on the Korean Peninsula.
Washington-Seoul relationship shaken by tariffs, funding disputes

"Right now, there is a problem of trust between the two governments," said Kim Sang-woo, a former politician with the left-leaning South Korean Congress for New Politics and now a member of the board of the Kim Dae-jung Peace Foundation.

A security and trade relationship that was previously considered secure has been rocked by tariffs, trade restrictions and demands from Washington that the South pay more for the US troops stationed in the country, Kim told DW.
President Lee's diplomats have lost access to key decision-making personnel in this White House, he added.

"I do not think this US administration is thinking long-term in the relationship with South Korea," Kim said. "They do not see South Korea as a part of their wider national security network and I do not think they are listening to experts on the importance of allies in the region."
"I also think that Trump is eager to meet with Kim because of his personal quest to obtain a Nobel Peace Prize."

Trump's widely publicized efforts to secure a Nobel have been thwarted so far. However, this might change if Trump somehow manages to formally end the Korean War that was put on hold by the 1953 armistice.
South Korea eyeing its own nuclear deterrent

"The most serious concern is that the US recognizes Pyongyang as a nuclear power, which would legitimize the North's program and undermine efforts to convince it to abolish its nuclear weapons as well as the broader non-proliferation system," said Lim Eun-jung, a professor of international studies at Kongju National University.

In parallel, she said, there are fears that Trump could reach an agreement with North Korea that requires it to scrap its long-range nuclear missiles — those that are capable of hitting targets in the United States — but permits it to retain short-range weapons that can still easily reach South Korea and Japan.

That would raise questions about the US commitment to defend South Korea in case of a nuclear attack. That uncertainty, in turn, is likely to give credence to voices arguing that South Korea needs to develop its own nuclear deterrent.

"For years, we have depended on US extended deterrence guarantees under the nuclear umbrella, but this US administration is unpredictable and there are more and more people asking why we don't just go it alone," Lim told DW.
"Virtually, all our neighbors have nuclear weapons, and while no-one wants the dominoes to start falling, it could happen."
Merz says Korean security affects Europe

The latest escalation between Seoul and Pyongyang comes amid repeated attempts by South Korean President Lee to improve communication with Pyongyang. The perceived outreach has irritated South Korea's European allies, who are angry over North Korea deploying soldiers and supplying munition and missiles to help Russia in the Ukraine war.
Why Kyiv and Seoul are clashing over North Korean POWs
Moscow is believed to be repaying Pyongyang's support with money, military technology and security guarantees.
During his visit to South Korea, Germany's Merz pointed out that "Korea's security affects Europe's security. And Europe's security also affects the security of Korea."
"The world is small — even in war," Merz added.
South Korea needs allies

Berlin, just like Seoul, has been disoriented by the Trump administration turning hostile on many of its allies while seeking reproachment with geopolitical rivals such as Russia and China. During his Asia tour, Merz pushed for an alliance of middle powers to protect free trade and oppose "unilateralism, autocratic power politics and violations of international law."

blocks.caption: German Chancellor Merz recently visited South Korea along with Japan and SingaporeImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "The fact remains that the United States is shifting its foreign policy, ⁠its foreign economic ​policy, and redefining its interests. As they do so, we must do the same," he said in South Korea.

It was not clear if Seoul will respond to Merz's appeal by moving closer to the European Union. At the moment, however, it seems apparent that the South Korean government is struggling to communicate with either North Korea or the US.
"It is a very difficult situation," said Kim Sang-woo. "There is no trust and no connections and that, to me, is very worrisome."
